newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Environment talks end in Harare, next in Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Environment talks end in Harare, next in Indonesia.

text.p: A 10-day Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species ended in Zimbabwe on Friday, and delegates chose to hold the next CITES conference in Indonesia in 1999.
The Harare conference was dominated by debate on a proposal by three southern African states to be exempted from a 1989 international ban in ivory trade.

The original application was fiercely opposed in the 138-member organisation, but a watered-down version was passed a day before the conference ended, allowing Botswana, Namibia and Zimbabwe to sell some ivory to Japan on an "experimental" basis in 1999 if their control measures satisfied CITES.
